No chat você digita, espera, copia e col: In chat, you type, wait, copy, and paste. If you close the window or the computer shuts down, the work in progress disappears. Ten tasks = ten waits with you in front.
O pedido é gravado antes de rodar. No in: The request is saved before it runs. In inemaccbot, the queue is a SQLite database on disk; in the homemade queue, it’s one file per task in a folder. Shut down? The task is still there.
Pega uma por vez: Picks up one at a time
Um trabalhador (worker) pega uma tarefa,: A worker picks up a task, hands it to the agent, and waits. If the process crashes midway, on the next startup it recovers what was in flight before accepting new work.
Cada tarefa termina num estado claro: de: Each task ends in a clear state: it worked (with the file or text) or it failed (with the reason). That’s what you check in the morning.
Rodar de novo só pega o que sobrou: Running it again only picks up what’s left
No inemaccbot o pedido chega pelo Telegr: In inemaccbot, the request comes through Telegram; in the homemade queue from lesson 3, it’s an .md file in a folder. The idea is the same.
Por que isso deixa você sair de perto: Why this lets you step away
Guardar antes de rodar, uma por vez, ret: Save before running, one at a time, resume after a crash, and separate done from failed: with these four guarantees, turning off the screen doesn’t cost you work.
O que você deve esperar de qualquer fila: What you should expect from any queue, homemade or otherwise.
O pedido vira registro em disco no momen: The request becomes a record on disk as soon as it arrives. It doesn’t depend on an open window or the program’s memory.
No inemaccbot, cada pedido vira um <b>jo: In inemaccbot, each request becomes a job in a database table. It has a number (j13), a queue, a status, and a number of attempts remaining.
Sinal no dia a dia: What this looks like day to day
Você manda o pedido pelo celular, o comp: You send the request from your phone, the computer restarts, and the request is still in the list.
Cada trabalhador pega uma tarefa, termin: Each worker picks up a task, finishes it, and only then picks up the next one. This keeps two jobs from competing for the same machine.
No inemaccbot há cinco filas com limites: In inemaccbot, there are five queues with different limits: the render queue runs one at a time on purpose because it uses the graphics card; the network queue accepts ten.
Se o processo cai no meio, a tarefa não: If the process crashes midway, the task isn’t lost or left half done forever. On the next startup, anything in progress goes back into the queue.
O inemaccbot faz isso antes de aceitar t: inemaccbot does this before accepting new work and writes to the log: boot: recuperação de leases — requeued=N failed=M. Requeued means it went back into the queue; failed means it had already used up all its attempts.
Tarefa que deu erro não some e não trava: A task that errors doesn’t disappear or block the queue: it goes to the failures side, with the reason recorded, and the queue moves on.
Os prompts do inemaccbot exigem que o ag: inemaccbot prompts require the agent to finish with RESULT: <path> or ERRO: <short reason>. This contract lets you know how each task ended without opening anything.
Os nomes mudam de uma fila para outra; a: The names change from one queue to another; the idea is the same.

O script e como usar: The script and how to use it
Está em ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh no r: It’s in ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh in the jornada-agentes repository. Both engines run through your subscription.
git clone https://github.com/inematds/jo:
git clone https://github.com/inematds/jornada-agentes.git
cd jornada-agentes
mkdir -p fila/entrada
echo "Summarize in 5 lines what a task queue is." > fila/entrada/01.md
echo "List 3 risks of leaving an agent running on its own." > fila/entrada/02.md
./ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh fila          # default engine: claude
./ferramentas/fila-caseira.sh fila codex    # or codex
mkdir -p \"$PASTA/entrada\" \"$PASTA/rod:
mkdir -p "$PASTA/entrada" "$PASTA/rodando" "$PASTA/feito" "$PASTA/falhou"

# resume: anything left in "rodando" (crash, Ctrl+C) goes back to the queue
for f in "$PASTA"/rodando/*.md; do [ -e "$f" ] && mv "$f" "$PASTA/entrada/"; done

for f in "$PASTA"/entrada/*.md; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "empty queue"; break; }
  nome=$(basename "$f")
  mv "$f" "$PASTA/rodando/$nome"          # picks up the task (only one at a time)
  saida=$(claude -p "$(cat "$PASTA/rodando/$nome")" < /dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$saida" ]; then
    # request + --- + response go to feito/
  else
    # request + ERROR (rc) + output go to falhou/
  fi
done
<ol><li>Cria as quatro pastas (rodar de:
1. Creates the four folders (running it again won’t break anything).
  2. Returns anything left in rodando/ to entrada/.
  3. Picks up one file at a time and moves it to rodando/ before calling the agent.
  4. Exit code 0 and a non-empty response: feito/. Otherwise: falhou/ with the exit code.
  5. At the end, counts how many are in each folder.

• Fixing it by hand without writing it down: the same failure comes back tomorrow.
  • Measuring only what failed: what matters is the share that was right the first time.

  • Restarting the bot while a task is still running to "clean up."
